G2533G.name: Caiaphas
G2533G.desc: High Priest living at the time of the New Testament
G2533G.brief: High priest during Jesus' ministry and trial
G2533G.short: Caiaphas, the high priest during Jesus' ministry, presided over Jesus' trial and played a key role in His crucifixion.

G2536G.name: Cainan
G2536G.desc: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
G2536G.brief: Son of Arphaxad, ancestor of Jesus (Luke's genealogy)
G2536G.short: Cainan, the son of Arphaxad, was an ancestor of Jesus Christ according to Luke's genealogy.

G2591.name: Carpus
G2591.desc: Man living at the time of the New Testament
G2591.short: Carpus was a friend of Paul in Troas, with whom Paul left his cloak, books, and parchments.

G2501M.name: Joseph
G2501M.desc: Man living at the time of the New Testament
G2501M.brief: Candidate to replace Judas as apostle
G2501M.short: Joseph, also called Barsabbas or Justus, was considered as a replacement for Judas among the apostles.

G2501J.name: Joseph
G2501J.desc: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
G2501J.short: Joseph, the son of Mattathias, is listed as an ancestor of Jesus Christ in Luke's genealogy.

G2501L.name: Joseph
G2501L.desc: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
G2501L.short: Joseph, the son of Jonam, is listed as an ancestor of Jesus Christ in Luke's genealogy.

G2501G.name: Joseph
G2501G.desc: Mary's husband living at the time of the New Testament
G2501G.brief: Husband of Mary and earthly father of Jesus
G2501G.short: Joseph was the husband of Mary and the earthly father of Jesus Christ.

G2501I.name: Joseph
G2501I.desc: Man living at the time of the New Testament
G2501I.brief: Of Arimathea, buried Jesus in his own tomb
G2501I.short: Joseph of Arimathea was a wealthy disciple who buried Jesus in his own new tomb.

G2500G.name: Joses
G2500G.desc: Man living at the time of the New Testament
G2500G.brief: Brother of Jesus and son of Mary
G2500G.short: Joses (or Joseph) was one of Jesus' brothers and a son of Mary.

G2500H.name: Joses
G2500H.desc: Man living at the time of the New Testament
G2500H.brief: Brother of James "the Less" and son of the "other" Mary
G2500H.short: Joses (or Joseph) was brother of James "the Less" who was an apostle.

G2542H.name: Caesarea
G2542H.brief: Coastal city, center of Roman rule in Judea
G2542H.short: Caesarea was a coastal city in Judea that served as a center of Roman administration.
G2542H.meaning: “city of Caesar,” named for Caesar Augustus

G2542G.name: Caesarea Philippi
G2542G.brief: City where Peter confessed Jesus as Messiah
G2542G.short: Caesarea Philippi was the location where Peter acknowledged Jesus as the Messiah and Son of God.

G2584.name: Capernaum
G2584.brief: Town in Galilee; center of Jesus' ministry
G2584.short: Capernaum was a fishing village on the Sea of Galilee that served as a center for Jesus' ministry in the region.

G2587.name: Cappadocia
G2587.brief: Region in Asia Minor; home to early Christian believers
G2587.short: Cappadocia was a region in Asia Minor where some early Christian believers lived.

G2570H.name: Fair Havens
G2570H.brief: Harbor on Crete; Paul's ship stopped during journey to Rome
G2570H.short: Fair Havens, a harbor on the island of Crete where Paul's ship stopped during his journey to Rome.

G2581.name: Zealot
G2581.brief: A member of a Jewish political faction
G2581.short: The Zealots were a Jewish political faction known for their fierce opposition to Roman rule and their advocacy for armed resistance (<ref="Matthew 10:4; Mrk.3.18">Matthew 10:4; Mrk.3.18</ref>).
